clue.text: Extent of pointless scene of conflict

indicators.note: point here is a compass point, so pointless says to drop the letter for north

parts.note: an arena is a scene of conflict, a place where battles or contests happen

explanation.surface: Someone surveys how far a futile battleground stretches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' removes N (north, a compass point) from ARENA.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe the size or range a space covers; an area is an extent of ground.

clue.text: Fool left with part of it

annotationWithheld.why: 'Fool left with part of it' (TWIT): no parse found in which 'left' gives letters; W (with) + IT needs a T that only 'part of it' could supply, reusing 'it'.
annotationWithheld.clue: Fool left with part of it

clue.text: Absolute freedom of a Scottish resort

parts.note: O as nil and BAN as prohibition read together as 'zero prohibition', which is total freedom

explanation.surface: Total liberty is the attraction of a Scottish holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the resort's name as O (zero) + BAN: having no prohibition at all is absolute freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a seaside town on Scotland's west coast, popular with holidaymakers and ferry passengers.

clue.text: I am taken in by Silas, a seaman

indicators.note: the letter is swallowed up inside the surname named next, so these words signal a container

parts.note: Silas Marner is the title character of George Eliot's novel, so Silas points to his surname

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being fooled by a man called Silas, a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: Silas Marner is George Eliot's weaver; 'am taken in by' puts I inside MARNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a sailor, someone who works at sea.

clue.text: Not far off earth and an explosion

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters of the words before it apart into a new order

explanation.surface: An explosion on the ground is uncomfortably close by.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close by in distance or time is not far off.

clue.text: Sketch sailor with a limp but achieve no result

parts.note: to sketch is to draw
AB is an able seaman, a sailor
limp hair is lank

explanation.surface: An artist sketches a sailor who walks with a limp, but the effort comes to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to search or try and find nothing, getting no result.

clue.text: Rex's girl in East Anglia

parts.note: rex is Latin for king, so Rex's means the king's
Lynn is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man named Rex has a girlfriend living in the east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: KING'S LYNN is a market town in Norfolk; East Anglia is the eastern bulge of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norfolk town lies in East Anglia, so the clue defines it by where it is.

clue.text: Cut for a group working together

explanation.surface: A haircut chosen for a team.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition stands for the first half of 'crew cut', a very short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a close-cropped haircut; a crew is also a team of people working together, as on a ship.

clue.text: Heavenly sea, it became rough in a confined space

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the small room, so in signals a container

parts.note: a cell is a small confined room

indicators.note: a sea that becomes rough is churned up, so its letters and those of it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heavenly sea turned choppy while someone was shut in a small room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'became rough' turns SEA + IT into ESTIA, which goes 'in' CELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial describes the sky or heaven, as in celestial bodies.

clue.text: Heed a military order

explanation.surface: Listen to a command shouted on the parade ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Attention means notice or heed; it is also the drill command to stand upright, heels together.

clue.text: Delia's content with a Biblical priest

indicators.note: the contents of a word are the letters held inside it

explanation.surface: A woman called Delia is pleased with a priest from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' reads as happy but means what Delia's holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli was the priest at Shiloh who raised Samuel in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Ancient city held in the continental bait

indicators.note: the city's name is gripped inside the French article, so held in signals a container

parts.note: le is French for the, so a continental the is LE
Ur was an ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: A ruined old city is being used as a trap by Europeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continental' means from mainland Europe, here French.
explanation.definitionFit: A lure is something used to attract and trap prey, like bait.

clue.text: Move on with an expression of surprise

explanation.surface: Urging something onward with a startled cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee is a command to a horse to go forward; it is also an exclamation of astonishment.

clue.text: Cultivators take some time in producing sensational stories

indicators.note: the farm machines take the time unit into themselves, so take signals a container

parts.note: tillers are people or machines that cultivate soil
HR is the abbreviation for hour, a period of time

explanation.surface: Farmers spend hours producing gripping tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some time' is vague, but an hour is a standard crossword piece of time; 'in producing' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrillers are exciting novels or films full of suspense.

clue.text: Height above which trees cannot grow

definitions.text: Height above which trees cannot grow

parts.words: Height above which trees cannot grow
parts.note: a plain description of the altitude on a mountain where forest gives way to bare ground

explanation.surface: A geography note about where woodland stops on a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: On mountains and in polar regions there is a limit of altitude or latitude beyond which no forest survives.

clue.text: Mr. Smith follows Cecil, one formerly from Zimbabwe

indicators.note: one name comes after the other, so follows orders the pieces

parts.note: Cecil Rhodes, the colonialist after whom Rhodesia was named
Ian Smith was the prime minister of Rhodesia

explanation.surface: A history note on two white leaders of the old colony.
explanation.walkthrough: Zimbabwe was called Rhodesia; Ian Smith led its government after Cecil Rhodes founded the colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Before independence Zimbabwe was Rhodesia, so someone from there was a Rhodesian.

clue.text: Held a sole kind of tenure

indicators.note: kind of suggests a loose version of the words before, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes a type of land holding involving a single fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sole' sounds like a fish, but it is just anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Leasehold is a form of property tenure where land is held under a lease for a set term.

clue.text: Place it in Kent

indicators.note: the small word sits within the abbreviation for the region, so in signals a container

parts.note: Kent lies in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put an object down in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in southeast England, giving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location, a place where something is or happens.

clue.text: Sinful or endless without time

indicators.note: without tells us to take the letter for time out of the longer word

parts.note: immortal means living for ever, endless

explanation.surface: A choice between wickedness and living forever outside time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoral behaviour breaks moral rules, which is what sinful means.

clue.text: Expressive about car Lily damaged

indicators.note: a damaged car is knocked out of shape, so its letters and the name with it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman called Lily gets emotional about the car she crashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical writing or speech expresses feeling with enthusiasm and imagination.

clue.text: A tea-drinker or non-believer

parts.note: thé is French for tea, and the suffix -ist marks a devotee, so a tea-drinker is spelt as tea plus devotee

explanation.surface: Someone who drinks tea is contrasted with an unbeliever.
explanation.walkthrough: THEIST is respelt as thé (French tea) + -ist; it really means a believer in God.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist is someone who rejects belief in any god.

clue.text: Present the girl's point

parts.note: her is the possessive for a girl
E (east) is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone offers a gift, making a point about the girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift; it is the adjective meaning in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: To be present is to be in this place, attending.

clue.text: Twisted confused mess in the end

indicators.note: the knot of string sits inside the final word, so in signals a container

parts.note: the end, simply END
a tangle is a confused mess

explanation.surface: In the end, a mess became knotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' is part of the definition of TANGLE, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Entangled things are twisted together and caught up.

clue.text: We hear of a good runner in West India

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is spoken, so its sound gives a differently spelt word

parts.note: a goer is something that runs well, as a car or horse

explanation.surface: Gossip about a fast horse in western India.
explanation.walkthrough: GOER said in a non-rhotic British accent sounds like GOA, a state on India's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Goa is a state on India's western coast, so it is located in West India.

clue.text: Note a hunting call cut short

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: soho is an old hunting cry on sighting a hare

explanation.surface: A hunter's cry is noted as being clipped.
explanation.walkthrough: SOH (or so) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: In tonic sol-fa, soh is the fifth note of the scale, a musical note.

clue.text: Potentially vile low lying ground

indicators.note: potentially says the word could become something else, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Low ground that could turn nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: VLEI is a South African word for a marshy hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: A vlei is a low-lying marshy area in South Africa that fills with water in wet seasons.

clue.text: More than 50 at Yemeni port are carrying too much

parts.note: over means more than
L is the Roman numeral for 50
Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: Ships at a Yemeni harbour hold over fifty tons too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Overladen means loaded beyond capacity, burdened with too much.

clue.text: Bird having fun

explanation.surface: A songbird enjoying itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The lark is a songbird such as the skylark; a lark is also a bit of fun or mischief.

clue.text: A small amount of soda to sadden the spirits

explanation.surface: A splash of soda is enough to cheer or depress someone's drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' suggests drinks beside soda, but here means mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash is a small splash of liquid; to dash someone's spirits or hopes is to depress them.

clue.text: Born and died in extreme poverty

parts.note: née means born, used before a woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: Someone's whole life spent destitute, from birth to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'in' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Need here is want or destitution, lacking the basics of life.

clue.text: Soon churchman loses his head

indicators.note: losing the head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral

explanation.surface: A clergyman is soon beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: ANON is an old word for soon, still used in 'see you anon'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon means shortly or in a little while.

clue.text: Died with heart strain most upset

indicators.note: the strain becomes the heart of the first word, so it is placed in the middle

parts.note: stress means strain

explanation.surface: Someone died of a heart strain, to everyone's great sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with heart' puts STRESS in the middle of DIED; it reads as heart trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Distressed means extremely upset, suffering anxiety or sorrow.
